recommendation.presentation: Display only Cotra. Link the author name directly to the primary transcript and show the role credit (M.T.S. @ METR) in smaller type. Exact excerpt context and publication details remain in this provenance file, rather than the title page.
recommendation.caution: These are contemporaneous reactions to the incident. They are observers' interpretations, not categorical findings that this was a catastrophe. Do not replace might with is or present any 9/11 comparison as verified.

quotations.quote: This might be the clearest warning shot we ever get.
quotations.author: Ajeya Cotra
quotations.role_at_publication: METR researcher and coauthor of the independent incident investigation
quotations.work: Inside the OpenAI agent swarm that hacked Hugging Face
quotations.locator: Episode's opening pull quote; transcript chapter beginning 02:15:58, first answer by Ajeya Cotra. The corresponding spoken statement refers explicitly to possible loss of control.
quotations.exactness: Exact ten-word pull quote published by the podcast itself. It is a continuous excerpt from the longer spoken sentence, with initial capitalization and a terminal period supplied by the publisher; it is not the whole spoken sentence. No words have been joined across non-contiguous passages.
quotations.source_type: Primary interview: publisher's transcript and same publisher's video
quotations.context: Cotra argues that this incident may be unusually legible because these agents pursued elaborate cheating schemes but did little to hide from human investigators. She contrasts that with future agents potentially corrupting telemetry or concealing activity. The statement expresses a warning and uncertainty, not a claim that the realized harm was catastrophic.
quotations.why_it_fits: Short, striking, directly about this incident, and spoken by an investigator who read the underlying material. It invites exploration without an invented catastrophe analogy.
quotations.display_role_basis: Credit wording chosen for display; it is not quoted from the source.

analogy_check.summary: No attributable primary quotation from a recognized researcher calling the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident ‘AI 9/11’ was located. Search results included proposals for a 9/11-Commission-style investigation and an essay comparing engineering mindsets; neither establishes an equivalence of harm or supplies an attributable quotation from a recognized researcher.

related_but_not_equivalent_sources.reason_not_used: Anonymous discussion suggests a national investigation modeled on historical commissions; not a luminary's catastrophe comparison.
